debates.motion: Does the Kalam cosmological argument show that the universe began to exist, has a cause, and points to a personal creator?

sections.title: Causation, Nothingness, and an Eternal Material Alternative
sections.rationale: This opening section follows the exchange over the Kalam’s causal premise, the disanalogy between ordinary and cosmic beginnings, and the proposed alternative of an eternal material series. Its 16 percent weight reflects the structural role of causation without displacing the debate’s larger finitude and creator exchanges.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section’s load-bearing statement of the causal principle and its nothing-from-nothing basis, making it structurally indispensable to the opening exchange.
This move supplies the principal early challenge by separating observed material rearrangements from an absolute beginning of material reality.
This reply clarifies the intended substance-level principle and develops the claimed explanatory significance of a uniquely cosmic beginning.
This move advances the quantified-language objection and identifies the risk of presupposing the causal principle under discussion.
This is the section’s load-bearing contrary construction, using nothing-from-nothing reasoning to motivate a beginningless material causal series.

sections.title: Actual Infinities and Hilbert’s Hotel
sections.rationale: This section gathers the first finitude argument and the sustained Hilbert’s Hotel exchange over part-whole intuitions, inconsistent principles, checkout cases, and relative complements. Its 27 percent weight reflects the breadth and central structural role of the actual-infinite route and its detailed opposition.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the load-bearing inference from the alleged impossibility of actual infinities to a finite past and a beginning of the universe.
This move introduces Hilbert’s Hotel as the principal concrete illustration supporting the actual-infinite line developed throughout the section.
This is the first direct challenge to the hotel illustration, distinguishing acknowledged strangeness from metaphysical impossibility.
This move gives the section’s load-bearing contrary account of infinite cardinality and explains why finite part-whole intuitions may not transfer.
This reply defends the use of metaphysical intuition and frames rejection of concrete actual infinities as a resolution of the inconsistent triad.
This move presents an alternative resolution of the triad by varying the application of principles in finite and infinite contexts.
This move extends the hotel exchange through checkout cases in which equal infinite removals are associated with different remainders.
This reply supplies the formal relative-complement treatment of the checkout cases and keeps the mathematical dispute explicit.
This rejoinder preserves the concrete arithmetic objection after the relative-complement reformulation and closes the hotel exchange.

sections.title: Successive Addition, Countdown, and Descending-Series Paradoxes
sections.rationale: This section contains the second finitude argument and the extended dispute over whether a beginningless sequence can terminate in the present. It includes the conditional, explanatory-timing, and Grim Reaper exchanges. Its 27 percent weight parallels the independent actual-infinite route’s structural scope.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the section’s load-bearing successive-addition inference from temporal formation to a finite and beginning-bearing past.
This is the section’s load-bearing contrary distinction between reaching an endless count’s end and reaching the end of a beginningless countdown.
This reply develops the question of why a beginningless countdown terminates today rather than at an earlier past point.
This move supplies a structurally central conditional analysis distinguishing necessary elapsed time from sufficient conditions for completion.
This reply reframes the timing question through a restricted, case-specific explanatory principle rather than a universal principle.
This move answers the timing demand with local predecessor explanations and distinguishes them from an ultimate explanation.
This rejoinder argues that citing the preceding count does not identify the contextually relevant factor behind completion today.
This move adds the Grim Reaper construction as an independent descending-series illustration within the successive-addition topic.

sections.title: Metric Time and the Scope of Temporal Beginning
sections.rationale: This compact section isolates the late clarification about what the finitude arguments establish: a beginning of metric time and the possible status of a non-metric or amorphous temporal reality. Its 10 percent weight recognizes a consequential scope issue while preserving proportion with the fuller exchanges.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move presents the section’s load-bearing non-metric-past alternative even after the preceding finitude arguments are provisionally granted.
This material concession and qualification fixes the direct scope of the metric-time conclusion and records the reply concerning amorphous time.

sections.title: Impersonal Indeterminism and Timeless Personal Agency
sections.rationale: This final section organizes the creator inference, the impersonal indeterministic alternative, and the dispute over whether changeless consciousness is coherent. Its 20 percent weight reflects the separate and explicit personhood component of the motion while retaining the earlier causal and finitude emphasis.

moveAssignments.rationale: This move states the section’s load-bearing impersonal indeterministic alternative to a personal origin of the universe.
This move provides the principal creator inference by contrasting a personal explanation with an eternal impersonal mechanism.
This reply adds the consciousness-based objection to a changeless personal agent outside an evolving causal order.
This closing reply addresses the freeze illustration and preserves the debate’s explicit treatment of timeless personhood.

bridgeMappings.rationale: The motion-level pro route is retained across the causal premise, the two independent finitude lines, and the concluding personal-cause inference, with each cited move assigned to the corresponding chronological section.
The pro central bridge is concentrated in the actual-infinity section, where the core temporal inference and its Hilbert-style supporting exchanges are retained together.
The concrete-actual-infinity subsidiary bridge is represented by the hotel illustration, the intuition defense, and both stages of the checkout-remainder argument in section 02.
The successive-addition subsidiary bridge is retained in section 03 through its constructive statement, countdown timing arguments, explanatory rejoinders, and the Grim Reaper illustration.
The personal-cause subsidiary bridge is represented in section 05 by the reply favoring personal explanation and the later defense of coherent timeless personhood.

The motion-level con route spans challenges to cosmic causation, actual infinity, successive addition, the scope of metric beginning, and personal agency, with all retained evidence mapped to its assigned section.

The con central bridge is preserved through the beginningless-material alternative and the distinct infinite-past, non-metric-time, and impersonal-origin alternatives distributed chronologically across the plan.
The con Hilbert’s Hotel subsidiary bridge is fully located in section 02 through the strangeness distinction, cardinality analysis, linguistic resolution, and relative-complement formulation.
The con successive-addition subsidiary bridge is represented in section 03 by the count-up/countdown asymmetry, conditional analysis, and local predecessor explanation.
The con impersonal-origin subsidiary bridge is retained in section 05 through the indeterministic mechanism alternative and the related objection to changeless personal consciousness.

debates.motion: Is belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God rational given alleged gratuitous evil, salvation confusion, rationality, design, and morality?

sections.title: Rational Belief and the Reliability of Human Reason
sections.rationale: Beginning with the debate’s definition of rational belief, this section groups the competing accounts of why human cognition can be trusted and the ensuing exchange over evolutionary truth-tracking and theistic reliability.

moveAssignments.rationale: This definition supplies the evidential standard that organizes the later dispute over whether theistic belief is rational rather than merely true or false.
This constructive states the principal theistic inference from reliable minds and an intelligible universe to an intelligent creator.
This move develops the evolutionary reliability challenge in full and distinguishes unguided evolution from a process intended by God to produce rational knowers.
This reply supplies two major structural objections: the separation of atheism from naturalism and the distinction between undermining an alternative and establishing theism.
This move provides the central evolutionary counteraccount, linking broadly accurate representation to the survival costs of systematically false beliefs.
This reply restates the contrast between truth as an intended cognitive function and truth as an intermittent correlate of evolutionary success.
This move completes the exchange by arguing that inaccessible divine reasoning creates an analogous reliability problem for the theistic account.

sections.title: Gratuitous Evil, Theodicy, and Restoration
sections.rationale: This section collects the initial evidential challenge from apparently purposeless suffering, the evil-God comparison, the concession about its significance, and the principal theistic accounts of normativity, afterlife, theodicy, and divine participation in suffering.

moveAssignments.rationale: This constructive introduces the debate’s principal suffering-based challenge by contrasting observed apparently gratuitous evil with the asserted divine attributes.
The evil-God comparison supplies a central probability test for possible reconciliations and develops the initial suffering argument beyond simple inconsistency.
This concession marks suffering as a central point of dispute while serving mainly as a transition into the con side’s substantive replies.
This reply introduces a normative contrast between Christianity’s account of a world that ought to be otherwise and a universe characterized by indifference.
This move adds the afterlife and possible restoration to the temporal frame within which earthly suffering is assessed.
This reply gathers the principal theodicy families and the claim of divine participation in suffering into the con side’s response structure.

sections.title: Salvation Confusion and the Identity of God
sections.rationale: This section connects the critique of disputed salvation conditions with the cumulative case for rational theism and the later contention that generic creator arguments do not by themselves identify an all-powerful, all-loving religious God.

moveAssignments.rationale: This constructive states the salvation-confusion problem through the combination of grave consequences and disagreement about the beliefs required for salvation.
This move develops the salvation critique by connecting hidden or disputed requirements with divine love, human access, and threatened punishment.
This constructive integrates the arguments from rationality, design, and morality into the con side’s cumulative motion-level case.
This reply directly addresses what the cumulative arguments could identify by separating a generic creator from the all-powerful, all-loving God under debate.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning and Evolutionary Accounts of Design
sections.rationale: This section places the cosmic fine-tuning argument alongside the later evolutionary account of apparent biological design, preserving the debate’s distinct but related explanations of ordered and life-permitting features.

moveAssignments.rationale: This constructive supplies the section’s principal design inference from narrow life-permitting physical conditions to intelligent calibration.
This move provides the pro side’s natural explanatory alternative for apparent biological design and locates its significance within changing available evidence.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Evolution, and Divine Goodness
sections.rationale: This section groups the moral argument for God, the evolutionary account of moral intuitions, and the extended exchange over whether goodness is independent of God, arbitrarily commanded, or grounded in the divine nature.

moveAssignments.rationale: This constructive states the principal moral argument by presenting objective moral obligation as requiring an explanation grounded in God.
This reply supplies an evolutionary account of care, sacrifice, moral intuition, and the emotional force of religious narratives.
This move introduces the section’s central dilemma concerning whether goodness exists independently of God or depends on divine command.
This reply adds the historical claim that biblical teaching about divine image-bearing helped furnish the moral standards used in the critique.
This move states the principal divine-nature response by grounding objective goodness in God rather than in an external standard or arbitrary command.
This reply completes the exchange by arguing that identifying God with goodness restates rather than removes the underlying dilemma.

bridgeMappings.rationale: The retained evidence spans the governing rationality standard, the principal challenges from suffering and salvation confusion, and the later argument about whether a creator can be identified with the God specified by the motion.

These moves preserve the structural comparison between evil and epistemic confusion on one side and the cumulative positive case on the other, including the dispute over what kind of deity that case could establish.

The mapping retains the full suffering exchange: apparently gratuitous evil, the evil-God comparison, the concession about its centrality, normative and afterlife replies, recognized theodicies, and the later divine-identity consequence.
Both retained moves are assigned together because they state and develop the same salvation-confusion line concerning severe consequences, disputed requirements, limited access, and divine love.

The retained evidence is distributed across the three relevant explanatory disputes: cognitive reliability, apparent design, and morality. Together those sections preserve the evolutionary and alternative-explanation material associated with this bridge.
The mapping retains the three constructive strands from reason, design, and morality as well as the move that explicitly combines them into the con side’s cumulative case concerning rational belief.

These retained moves preserve every component of the cumulative structure: reason, fine-tuning, morality, their explicit combination, and the concession and replies intended to keep suffering within the same overall evidential comparison.

All retained evidence for this bridge is grouped in the rationality section, including the unguided-evolution challenge, the guided-evolution contrast, and the successive evolutionary and parity-based replies.

The mapping places the fine-tuning constructive and the evolutionary account of apparent design in the design section while retaining the later creator-identity reply in the section addressing what such arguments could establish.

The morality section retains the objective-morality constructive, evolutionary alternative, divine-command dilemma, historical biblical account, divine-nature response, and final restatement objection as one complete topical exchange.

debates.motion: Does the evidence from cosmology, fine-tuning, morality, Jesus' resurrection, and religious experience make Christian theism more reasonable than skeptical atheism?

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning, Causation, and a Personal Creator
sections.rationale: This opening section follows the earliest exchange from the universe's beginning and causal explanation through the proposed attributes and personality of its cause, including the later scientific, causal, and infinity-focused replies. Its weight reflects the number and structural depth of the linked cosmological steps.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive chain from a finite beginning to a transcendent cause and its proposed nonphysical attributes.
This supplies the separate load-bearing step from a nonphysical cause to an unembodied mind and personal creator.
This is a principal challenge to extending ordinary causal experience from material rearrangement to creation from nothing.
This major scientific reply addresses whether current cosmology establishes an absolute beginning rather than merely a beginning of expansion.
This major reply addresses the distinct inference from a nonphysical cause to a substrate-independent mind.
This major counter-reply returns to the cosmological evidence and the claimed scope of the Borde-Guth-Vilenkin theorem.
This major counter-reply develops the causal-principle exchange concerning efficient and material causes.
This major reply addresses the philosophical argument against an actual infinite through the arithmetic of infinite collections.
This major counter-reply completes the selected exchange about infinite subtraction and physically instantiated collections.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Alternative Explanations, and Designer Specificity
sections.rationale: This section begins with the fine-tuning constructive and follows the exchange over cosmic probabilities, deeper physics, multiverse alternatives, and what properties a designer inference could establish. The weight represents a distinct evidential line with several independent structural questions.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive comparison among physical necessity, chance, and design.
This concession marks supporting common ground about when fine-tuning would invite a designer explanation.
This is a principal multi-part reply concerning probability, deeper physical explanation, and multiverse scenarios.
This major reply raises the separate specificity issue of whether fine-tuning identifies a morally perfect Christian God.
This major counter-reply addresses both parameter-range probabilities and the cumulative role of separate evidential arguments.
This concession clarifies the limited divine attribute attributed to the selected evidential arguments.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Divine Character, and the Evidence of Evil
sections.rationale: This section starts with the moral constructive, then groups the exchange over whether objective value requires God, how naturalism might ground value and obligation, and whether evil fits a perfect deity. Its weight reflects the interaction between a positive moral line and a distinct contrary-evidence line.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive route from objective moral values to a divine ground.
This major reply separates apprehension of objective value and intrinsic human worth from belief in God.
This major counter-reply develops the questions of nonarbitrary value and binding moral obligation under naturalism.
This is the load-bearing contrary-evidence move connecting observed evil and purported divine morality to expectations about a perfect God.
This major reply supplies a proposed purpose-based explanation for permitting natural and moral evil.

sections.title: Resurrection Evidence and Historical Sources
sections.rationale: This section isolates the resurrection line because it turns on a distinctive historical record: the empty tomb, appearances, disciples' belief, source dependence, discrepancies, and historian agreement. Its weight reflects an independent route to specifically Christian theism with a compact direct exchange.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the section's load-bearing constructive inference from three claimed historical facts to resurrection.
This major reply addresses dating, authorship, source dependence, and discrepancies in the Gospel evidence.
This major counter-reply focuses the historical exchange on scholarly acceptance of the three selected facts.

sections.title: Religious Experience, Rival Hypotheses, and the Cumulative Burden
sections.rationale: This final section begins with personal religious experience and follows the chronological exchange over religious disagreement, competing hypotheses, the required comparative case, and absence-of-evidence reasoning. Its weight reflects its role in connecting one evidential line to the debate's cumulative and motion-level framing.

moveAssignments.rationale: This is the load-bearing constructive presentation of immediate personal experience as an independent way of knowing God.
This major reply uses conflicting religious outcomes to question the reliability of shared belief-forming sources.
This load-bearing constructive sets the comparative burden among the specific Christian claim and numerous rival hypotheses.
This major counter-reply disputes the claim of one common religious method and restates the combined evidential method.
This major counter-reply addresses the expectation needed for absence of evidence to count against God's existence.

bridgeMappings.rationale: The motion-level route is retained through its five constructive evidential lines, each assigned to the chronological topical section devoted to that line and its exchange.
The cumulative convergence bridge is represented across all five sections by the principal constructive lines and later moves connecting those lines to rival hypotheses and contrary evidence.
The finite-beginning and transcendent-cause bridge is concentrated in section-01 through its constructive causal steps and retained replies about cosmology, causation, and actual infinity.
The design-from-fine-tuning bridge is retained in section-02 through the initial necessity-chance-design comparison and the later defense of probability and multiple fine-tuning cases.
The resurrection bridge is retained in section-04 through the three-fact constructive inference and the later historical reply concerning scholarly acceptance of those facts.
The contrary motion-level route is retained through the comparative rival-hypothesis framework in section-05 and the empirical argument from evil and divine character in section-03.
The central skeptical route spans all five sections through retained challenges to causal, fine-tuning, moral, resurrection, experiential, and specifically Christian inferences.
The skeptical Kalam bridge is concentrated in section-01 through the retained challenges concerning creation from nothing, an absolute beginning, an unembodied mind, and actual infinity.
The skeptical fine-tuning bridge is retained in section-02 through the conditional concession, probability and alternative-explanation cautions, and designer-specificity challenge.
The contrary-evidence bridge from evil and opaque divine presence is retained in section-03 through the move comparing the observed world and purported divine morality with a perfect God.
